question: Define surface tension and mention factors affecting it.
gold_answer:
# Introduction

---

## Definition

Surface tension is the property of a liquid surface that causes it to behave like a stretched elastic membrane, minimizing its surface area. 

This behavior is caused by cohesive forces, as liquid molecules at the surface experience a net inward pull from the molecules beneath them.

---

## Factors Affecting Surface Tension

* **Temperature Inversion:** Raising the temperature increases the kinetic energy of the molecules, weakening cohesive bonds and reducing surface tension.
* **Chemical Impurities:** Adding highly soluble materials like salt increases surface tension, whereas adding surfactants like soap lowers it significantly.

---

## Formula

The surface tension scalar definition is given by:

$$T = \frac{F}{L}$$

Where:
* $T$ represents the surface tension factor
* $F$ represents the force acting parallel to the surface along a line segment
* $L$ represents the total length of the line segment over which the force acts

---

## Summary

Surface tension arises from unbalanced molecular attraction at a liquid's surface, causing it to minimize its area. This property decreases with heat and surfactant additives.

# Surface Tension
📖 Quick Definition
Surface Tension is the property of a liquid surface that makes it behave like a stretched elastic membrane, due to the net inward cohesive force acting on surface molecules.

It is defined as the force per unit length acting along the surface of a liquid, perpendicular to any imaginary line drawn on the surface.
⚗️ Main Formula
$$T = \frac{F}{L}$$
TSurface Tension (N/m)
FForce acting on the surface (N)
LLength of the line on the surface (m)
💡 Physical Interpretation
  • Molecules inside a liquid are pulled equally in all directions → zero net force.
  • Molecules at the surface have fewer neighbors above → net inward pull.
  • This inward pull causes the surface to contract and minimize its area.
SI Unit: N/m  |  CGS Unit: dyne/cm  |  Dimensions: [MT⁻²]
---
⚙️ Factors Affecting Surface Tension
🌡️ Temperature
As temperature increases, cohesive forces between molecules weaken.
↓ Surface Tension decreases with rise in temperature
Exception: Molten cadmium and copper show an increase.
🧪 Impurities / Solutes
  • Soluble impurities (e.g., NaCl, sugar) → ↑ Increase surface tension
  • Sparingly soluble impurities (e.g., soap, detergent) → ↓ Decrease surface tension
Surfactants like soap drastically reduce surface tension — used in cleaning.
🔗 Nature of Liquid
Liquids with stronger intermolecular (cohesive) forces have higher surface tension.
Mercury — High ST Alcohol — Low ST
⚡ Electrification
When a liquid is electrified, charges on the surface repel each other, causing the surface to expand.
↓ Surface Tension decreases on electrification
🌊 Presence of Dissolved Gas
Dissolved gases in a liquid reduce cohesion between molecules.
↓ Surface Tension decreases with dissolved gases
🫧 Contamination / Surface Films
Oil films or dust on the surface reduce intermolecular attraction at the surface layer.
↓ Surface Tension decreases with surface contamination
---
📋 Quick Summary Table
| Factor | Effect on Surface Tension | |---|---| | Increase in Temperature | ↓ Decreases | | Soluble impurities (NaCl) | ↑ Increases | | Surfactants (Soap) | ↓ Decreases | | Electrification | ↓ Decreases | | Dissolved Gases | ↓ Decreases | | Stronger cohesive forces | ↑ Increases |
